lines: A dual-voice bytebeat synthesiser running the Keeos Ogham hardware module's own firmware: each voice plays one of a hundred short integer formulas on a shared time base
Sets Parameter A, a number from 0 to 255 that both voices read; what it changes depends on the formula each voice is running
Sets Parameter B, a number from 0 to 255 that both voices read; what it changes depends on the formula each voice is running
Sets the playback rate: free running it goes from a sixty-fourth of speed at fully counter-clockwise through unity at noon to sixty-four times at fully clockwise
A lo-fi macro that is clean at the centre: turned down it filters and folds, turned up it crushes and adds resonance
Says what the Clk/VOct jack carries: at Clk it is a clock that drives the time base, and at VOct it is a pitch at a volt per octave
Added to the A knob, a fifth of the knob's travel per volt, with the total held between the ends; the CV to Tone field can take it away from A and point it at the Tone macro
Added to the B knob, a fifth of the knob's travel per volt, with the total held between the ends; the CV to Tone field can take it away from B and point it at the Tone macro
A rising edge above 1V puts the time base back to zero and plucks the low-pass gate, which is silent unless the LPG decay field is above zero
A clock the time base follows, or a pitch at a volt per octave, according to the Clk/VOct switch; in VOct mode no edges are taken from it at all
Voice 1 after the tone macro, the effects chain and the low-pass gate, 5V at full scale and a little over on peaks
Voice 2 after the tone macro, the effects chain and the low-pass gate, 5V at full scale and a little over on peaks
An envelope follower on one of the two voices, or that voice's bytebeat straight out as a voltage, 0-10V; the CV Out mode field picks which of the four
A 10V gate following the tempo the module works out for itself from voice 1's rhythm
Note — turning the Func encoder changes the function of the selected voice, a click swaps which voice is selected, and holding it about 0.6 seconds opens the Menu and leaves it
Note — the Func encoder is not a Rack parameter, so clicking it cannot reach this help and Rack's MIDI mapper cannot reach the two function slots; the right-click menu lists every function by name
Note — the scroll wheel turns the Func encoder only while Rack's own Scroll wheel knob adjustment preference is on, and a drag turns it unless Drag turns the encoder is switched off
Note — the display reads the selected voice and its function as X-NN, and in the Menu the effect, field and value as T x. NN; the dot at the far right means the Tone macro is at its clean centre
Note — with a clock patched into Clk the Rate knob snaps to a division or multiplication of it, a thirty-second up to thirty-two times; pulling the cable holds that rate until the knob moves
Note — with the switch at VOct the Rate knob becomes a fine tune of one octave either way, added to the pitch input, and the formula is played faster or slower rather than restarted
Note — the last function in the bank is a 440Hz reference tone, and while a voice is on it that voice runs at unity whatever the Rate knob, the clock or the pitch input say
Note — the module is monophonic: every jack is read and written as a single channel
Menu — Voice 1 function — picks voice 1's formula from the whole bank by name, grouped as Textural, Noise, Percussive, Rhythmic and Melodic, with the 440Hz reference at the end
Menu — Voice 2 function — picks voice 2's formula from the whole bank by name, grouped as Textural, Noise, Percussive, Rhythmic and Melodic, with the 440Hz reference at the end
Menu — Drag turns the encoder — lets a mouse drag over the Func encoder turn it; the setting is kept for this computer rather than in the patch
Menu — Open the Menu — does what holding the Func encoder does, and reads Leave the Menu while the Menu is open
Menu — Settings — shows all 22 Menu fields at once with their values, instead of walking them four digits at a time
Menu — FX chain: Off, On — switches the whole three-stage effects chain in and out
Menu — Chain topology: Serial, Parallel — wires the chorus, flanger and phaser one after another, or side by side
Menu — Chorus level — sets how much chorus is mixed in, 0 to 99, and 0 skips the stage entirely
Menu — Chorus type: Clean, Ensemble — one chorus voice, or three detuned ones
Menu — Chorus rate — sets how fast the chorus sweeps, 0 to 99
Menu — Chorus depth — sets how far the chorus sweeps, 0 to 99
Menu — Flanger level — sets how much flanger is mixed in, 0 to 99, and 0 skips the stage entirely
Menu — Flanger type: Clean, Barber-pole — a sweep that turns round at each end, or one that only ever climbs
Menu — Flanger rate — sets how fast the flanger sweeps, 0 to 99; 50 stops a barber-pole sweep
Menu — Flanger feedback — sets how much of the flanger's output goes back into it, 0 to 99
Menu — Phaser level — sets how much phaser is mixed in, 0 to 99, and 0 skips the stage entirely
Menu — Phaser type: Clean, Bi-phase — four poles, or eight poles with a second sweep
Menu — Phaser rate — sets how fast the phaser sweeps, 0 to 99
Menu — Phaser 2nd LFO — sets the second sweep's ratio to the first in Bi-phase, 0 to 99
Menu — CV Out mode: Envelope of Out 1, Envelope of Out 2, Out 1 as DC, Out 2 as DC — chooses what the CV Out jack carries
Menu — CV slew rise — slows how fast the CV Out can rise, from off up to about 5 seconds
Menu — CV slew fall — slows how fast the CV Out can fall, set apart from the rise
Menu — CV hold: Off, 2 ticks, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256 — samples the CV Out and holds it for that many ticks, in the two DC modes only
Menu — LPG decay — sets how long the low-pass gate takes to close after a Sync pluck, 0 switching it off and 1 to 99 running 2ms to 20 seconds
Menu — CV to Tone: Off, CV A, CV B — takes one of the two CV inputs off its parameter and uses it to modulate the Tone macro
Menu — Parameter smoothing: Off, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128 — crossfades A and B across a grid of that many steps rather than changing them at once
Menu — Out 2 drone: Coupled, Frozen — freezes voice 2 at its current rate and parameters so it runs on independently of the knobs

Ogham.notes: Read at the v2.0.0 tag, commit fdc34da. Every commit in the repository carries version 2.0.0, since plugin.json has been touched once, so the tag is what settles which source describes the shipped binary; the fourteen commits after it are CI, documentation and two static-analysis fixes, and the whole delta was checked line by line for behaviour. It changes no name, no value and nothing in the audio path: Median3 is rewritten to the same function, the FX save and load walk the same four bytes through an array of pointers instead of pointer arithmetic, an #error becomes a static_assert, and the vendored firmware sync to 1.17 adds default initialisers the maker records as leaving the firmware byte-identical. No user-visible string differs between the two ends, so both describe this module identically. Two parameters have no widget at all: FUNC1_PARAM and FUNC2_PARAM, the per-voice function slots, are configured and read but never added to the panel, because on the hardware the Func encoder is the only way to them. They are absent from paramPos, so no click can reach them, and they get no line and no tag; the encoder itself is a plain Widget rather than a ParamWidget and is equally unreachable, so what it does is written as Notes. Every configInput and configOutput is called once with its own enum. Widget order does not follow enum order: the params are added as MODE, RATE, A, B, TONE - indices 6, 4, 2, 3, 5 - and the four input jacks run CV A, CV B, Clk/VOct, Sync across the panel, which is indices 0, 1, 3, 2, since the enum declares SYNC before CLK_VOCT while the production legends put Clk third. Tagged from the widget positions. The Clk/VOct input is left without a family: the Clk/VOct switch makes it either a clock or a 1V-per-octave pitch, so either colour would be wrong half the time. The maker's README and the code agree throughout; the numbers in the lines come from OghamApp.cpp - MapKnobToRate as two to the power of twelve times the knob minus six, giving a sixty-fourth to sixty-four times, CLOCK_RATIO_MAX_EXP of 5 giving a thirty-second to thirty-two times, VOCT_KNOB_SPAN_OCT of 2 giving an octave either way, and the LPG decay range from the field's own detail text.
